messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing steady KV cache memory growth on H100 when long contexts hit our paged slab allocator. Looks like fragmentation + remap aliasing over time. Posting traces shortly.

kevin: Can you paste the minimal repro and which image/commit?

maria: repro: small harness using llama2-13b quantized, seq=32k, batch=1 on h100-2. Commit: runtime@a3b7f2. Quick command we used:
```
./run_longctx_repro --model llama2-13b --seq 32768 --gpu h100 --longctx 65536 --seed 42
```
Log excerpt shows PT entries growing without corresponding evicts:
```
[KV] pt_entries=102400 alloc=2048 evict_ops=512
[KV] pt_entries=118752 alloc=2048 evict_ops=530
[KV] pt_entries=136128 alloc=2048 evict_ops=531
```

jordan: interesting. on A100 iirc we saw evict_ops climb in lockstep with pt_entries, but h100 traces look like evict completions are delayed. Could be async-evict ordering bug or we fail to reclaim shadow slots at stripe boundaries.

anya: saw something similar on mi250 where memcpy between host and device stalls caused backlog, but that was NVLink related on Nvidia. For MI we saw a different pattern: fragmented slab buckets that never coalesced. Link to my flame: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/9876 :eyes:

kevin: can you try running with coalescing disabled? patch ENV: KV_COALESCE=0 and set KV_DEBUG_SHADOW=1, also try KV_EVICT_BATCH=64 to force more aggressive evict.

maria: ran with KV_COALESCE=0 and KV_EVICT_BATCH=64. PT entries still grow but slower. Attached small debug dump:
```
# summary after 10k tokens
pt_total=129536
free_slots=1024
slab_frag_ratio=0.73
reuse_window_avg=2384
stale_owner_count=112
```

sre-bot: perf-runner: job 98234 queued for slots h100-2, a100-1, mi250-0 (CI tag: kvcache-longctx).

jordan: hypothesis: when remap happens at slab stripe boundary we sometimes create a ghost PT entry that keeps the owner bit set but free list link is dropped. Over repeated remaps those ghosts accumulate and increase reuse_window and prevent coalesce. Stale_owner_count in dump matches that. This would explain arch diff: different DMA remap granularity on H100 vs A100/MI.

anya: I'll repro on MI250 tomorrow and instrument the page-walk path to log owner transitions. If it's ghost entries, we should be able to reproduce with a tightly crafted remap pattern.

kevin: sgtm. I'll open a tracking ticket (INF-4444) and attach the trace + dump. Can someone add a minimal patch that 1) asserts owner==valid before reuse and 2) adds a counter when free_list drop occurs? That should surface root cause quickly. :shipit:

maria: added minimal repro and gdb trace to INF-4444, linked the perf runs and my raw dump. Thanks all — will run the coalesce=0 matrix across h100/a100/mi250 and report back. :thumbsup:
